newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: LITHUANIA C.BANK BACKS SLOW END TO CURRENCY PEG.
newsitem.headline: LITHUANIA C.BANK BACKS SLOW END TO CURRENCY PEG.

text.p: The central bank of the Baltic state of Lithuania on Thursday said an end to the country's currency peg arrangement and the return to a fully-functioning central bank should be slow and carefully considered.

The litas is set at four to one dollar under a currency board, which means the bank's foreign currency reserves have to back the local currency in circulation. But it also strips the central bank of all the usual monetary tools and powers.
"We were all the time in favour of returning all the normal functions to the central bank," Bank of Lithuania governor Reinoldijus Sharkinas told a news conference.
"We are getting ready so the central bank will be prepared to carry out those functions, but not overnight," he added.
"We have to be well prepared and foresee all the possible variants in this decision," Sharkinas said.
Lithuania's new right-wing government has pledged to scrap the currency peg and introduce a freely-floating currency. It has said this can come about in around 18 months.
The currency board stops the bank printing money that cannot be backed by reserves and has helped bring down inflation.
The central bank is left to oversee the functioning of the currency board but has none of the other powers such as market interventions or interest rate changes.
Sharkinas said there would be no sudden changes and that all would be done in the open and only under the right conditions.

"First of all we have totally restore trust into the banking system and now there are only the first signs," he said, noting that bank deposits were increasing, bank capital was strengthening and liquidity was improving.
"But now these are only the first signs and the conditions to improve their (banks) work," he said.

He said officials in the central bank were already studying how best to make the change over to a floating currency and a fully-functioning central bank and would continue to do so. -- Riga Newsroom, +371 721 5240
